notes: THE NET WORTH AND DASHBOARD PAGES WERE DISCARDING SCENARIO-OWNED PROPERTY. REPORTED: with a Rs 1 crore land scenario enabled, net worth at 2052 fell from Rs 31 crore to Rs 28.4 crore — the purchase reducing net worth by roughly the cash spent, exactly the behaviour v2026.05.09.01 was meant to end. DIAGNOSED: the engine's p.netWorth did contain the asset. But neither page uses p.netWorth. Both rebuild net worth from parts, because they need the corrected savings chain rather than the engine's raw cashSeries, and each did so with its own inline expression: 'inv + adjustedCashSeries[i] + liab' on the Net Worth page and 'inv + cash + liab' on the Dashboard. Neither added scAssetSeries or scLiabSeries. The asset was computed correctly by the engine and then dropped on the way to the screen. FIXED with a single shared function, sharedNetWorthSeries(p), now used by both: investments + savings chain + liabilities + scenario-owned property + the loan still owed on it. Verified on the reported scenario: day one minus Rs 56,667, matching the engine exactly and equal to one month's interest on the borrowed amount; April 2041 minus Rs 9.09 lakh while the loan is still mostly interest; April 2051 plus Rs 23.46 lakh once the last EMI clears; December 2052 PLUS Rs 36.09 lakh against the Rs 2.6 crore drop previously shown. The page figures differ slightly from p.netWorth in later months, by design — the pages use the corrected savings chain and p.netWorth uses the raw engine cash, so the page figure is the more accurate of the two. THIS IS THE SIXTH INDEPENDENT COMPUTATION of a shared quantity found in this codebase, after four separate month-end cash calculations unified across v2026.05.08.01 and .02. The pattern is consistent: a page needs a corrected version of an engine value, writes its own inline expression, and then misses every later change to the underlying model. Using one named function rather than repeating an expression is the only thing that has reliably prevented recurrence. ALSO WORTH KNOWING, not a bug: a 20-year loan at 8.5% against land appreciating at 6% runs NEGATIVE for roughly the first twelve to fifteen years, because early EMIs are overwhelmingly interest and interest is a genuine loss while principal merely converts cash to equity. The crossover on the reported scenario falls in the mid-2040s. A horizon ending before then shows only the losing half of the curve. Regression confirms the Projection-to-Dashboard and Decisions-to-chain gaps both remain zero. No page errors.
